transcript: So in finance, month-end is basically the answer to this question, because everything is urgent at the same time. The way I think about it is, I ask what breaks if this is one day late, and for whom. Payroll and supplier payments on the due date, those come first, because a late salary hurts a real person and a late supplier payment costs us penalties. Then anything feeding the board pack, because leadership makes decisions on it. Internal reconciliations that nobody reads until next week can wait a day. Um, a concrete one: last quarter the CEO asked for a cash forecast the same afternoon the auditors asked for supporting documents and payroll was due the next morning. I did payroll first, forty minutes. Then I called the auditor, told them they'd get the documents at noon the next day, and asked if that blocked them. It didn't. Then I did the forecast. What I've learned is to tell people when they'll get it, before they have to chase me. Most people are fine waiting if they know when.
